subject: Preserve-rate proposal: tiered annual prepay with staged ramp
messages:
From: Ellie Robinson <ellie@fintechscale.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@fintechscale.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: pricing exposure & prepay options

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well — our renewal for the Redwood inference contract is coming up in Q3 and we’re reviewing options to avoid the year-over-year increases we’ve seen with other vendors. Procurement asked me to see whether Redwood can offer a multi-year prepay structure to lock current rates, but we need something that also aligns with our internal budget phasing (we ramp spend over the first 9–12 months of each year).

High level asks:
- Can Redwood lock pricing for 2–3 years with a prepay?
- Are there ramp schedules or credits if our quarterly consumption ramps in Y1?
- Any accounting treatments or PO requirements we should plan for?

We’re targeting a decision by end of June to get finance to budget for a July PO. Can you share options and a draft SOW/pricing so we can start procurement review?

Thanks,
Ellie Robinson
Head of Cloud Ops
FinTechScale

Attachment: (requested) current usage snapshot - not attached here
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Robinson <ellie@fintechscale.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing exposure & prepay options

Ellie — thanks for the clear ask. Appreciate the timeline.

Short answer: yes, we can structure a multi-year prepay that preserves current unit rates and includes staged ramp credits to accommodate front-loaded or ramped consumption. I’ll outline two practical options below that we commonly use and then follow up with a formal proposal/SOW.

Option A — 36-month tiered prepay (price lock):
- 3-year prepay at 85% of list (effectively ~15% discount), invoiced annually or upfront (customer choice)
- Staged ramp credit: if Y1 usage is <= 60% of committed annual units, we apply a carry-forward credit pool to Y2; if usage > committed, normal consumption billing applies
- Benefit: strongest price protection, predictable unit economics for your finance team

Option B — 24-month blended prepay with ramp banding:
- 2-year commit at 90% of list with quarterly true-ups and a predefined ramp band (30/35/35)
- If you exceed band in Q1, we offer a one-time ramp credit to smooth to Q2

Notes and open items for procurement:
- We can accommodate staggered invoicing (annual vs. full upfront) and produce a PO-friendly SOW and invoice schedule.
- For accounting: prepay can be treated as prepaid expense; we provide invoice schedules and SOW references for your accounting team.

I’m attaching a short draft proposal with numbers and a sample SOW for PO ingestion. If useful I can loop in Marissa from sales ops to confirm finance-friendly invoice language.

Next steps: I’ll pull a formal tiered proposal and a DocuSign-ready SOW by COB Tuesday. Can you confirm whether procurement prefers annual invoices or a single upfront invoice?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Tiered_Prepay_Options_v1.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-24T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FTS negotiation strategy & approval ask

Marissa / Lauren — moving this forward with FinTechScale (Ellie). Procurement is asking for price protection and an approach that doesn’t require a huge cash hit in Y1. Recommended commercial concession:

Proposal I want approval to offer to procurement:
- 36-month prepay commitment, list discounted to 82% (18% net discount) if they sign a DocuSign within 30 days of proposal delivery
- Payment profile: customer selects annual invoicing for FYs 1–3 (rather than full upfront), Redwood issues invoice at start of each year with the price lock applied
- Ramp accommodation: if Y1 consumption < 70% of committed units, issue a carry-forward credit equal to unused committed units (usable in Y2); no cash refunds
- Early-exit protection: 6-month notice, remaining prepay value converted to 60% repayable credit to be applied to future invoices (protects Redwood economics)

Rationale: gives them price lock and mitigates finance objections by avoiding single large upfront payment while still securing multi-year revenue. Margin hit is manageable if we attach the early-exit language.

Request: approval to include 18% discount and annual invoicing option. If approved, I’ll finalize proposal doc and send to Ellie with a DocuSign and a PO-ready SOW.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Robinson <ellie@fintechscale.com>, procurement@fintechscale.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Updated: Tiered prepay proposal + staged ramp credits (DocuSign ready)

Hi Ellie / team — attached is the proposal we discussed and a PO-ready SOW. Key points summarized below so procurement can review quickly:

What we’re offering (summary):
- 36-month tiered prepay, price locked at 82% of current list for committed units across term
- Invoicing: annual invoicing by default (option for full upfront if preferred)
- Staged ramp credits: unused committed units in Y1 carry forward to Y2 as credit pool; example table included in attachment
- Early-exit protection and conversion language included in SOW (to address internal finance concerns)

Attachments: FTS_Prepay_Tiered_Proposal_v3.pdf, SOW-FinTechScale-2027.xlsx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/FTS-SIG-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FTS-46

Can you confirm:
1) Procurement preference for annual invoicing vs full upfront?
2) Target date for final signature / PO so we can reserve capacity under this pricing? We can hold the price for signature by 2027-07-15.

If procurement wants a short call to review the invoice schedule, I’m happy to join with Lauren and Marissa.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: FTS_Prepay_Tiered_Proposal_v3.pdf, SOW-FinTechScale-2027.xlsx

Date: 2027-06-30T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated: Tiered prepay proposal + staged ramp credits (DocuSign ready)

Priyom — thank you, this looks workable. A few quick sync notes (procurement):

- FinTechScale approves the 36-month prepay at the 82% rate conditional on the annual invoice schedule in the SOW.
- We will route the DocuSign and PO through finance but need one small change: a 30-day extension on the signature deadline, so price hold until 2027-08-14. Can you confirm?
- Please confirm the example table for Y1 carry-forward credits will be included in the SOW (we saw it in the PDF).

On the logistics: I’ll prepare the PO once we have the final SOW with invoice milestones and the adjusted signature hold date. Send final DocuSign link and I’ll route it through legal/finance.

Thanks,
Raj Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
FinTechScale
